paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God is holy, and sin is serious. That's why Aaron couldn't just wander behind that veil whenever he felt like it, and the LORD said why: "I appear in the cloud above the mercy seat." (Lev 16:2) Nobody walks into that kind of holiness casually, and I think that should slow us down a little.

But look at what else this passage shows. God doesn't just say "stay away." He gives a way for sin to be dealt with, so He can keep dwelling among His people. The Tent of Meeting "abides among them in the midst of their impurities." (Lev 16:16) And the live goat "will carry on itself all their iniquities into a solitary place." (Lev 16:22) That's God making a way for sin to be carried off, and for His people to be clean again.

And the LORD says it plainly: "on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, and you will be clean from all your sins before the LORD." (Lev 16:30) Notice who needed it, friend. Aaron had to make atonement for himself first (Lev 16:6), so nobody gets to skip this. It reminds me why I thank Jesus, the Lamb, every day. He is the One who gave His life to rescue people from the dark and bring them home (Mark 10:45), and I know what it's like to be found.
